title: Move the grid yourself

sliders.name: a
sliders.label: a: x-coordinate of where î lands

sliders.name: b
sliders.label: b: x-coordinate of where ĵ lands

sliders.name: c
sliders.label: c: y-coordinate of where î lands

sliders.name: d
sliders.label: d: y-coordinate of where ĵ lands

prompts: Start at a=2, b=−1, c=1, d=1. The green î arrow lands on (2,1), the first column (a,c); the red ĵ arrow lands on (−1,1), the second column (b,d).
The yellow arrow is where the input vector (1,2) lands. Predict it first: 1·(2,1) + 2·(−1,1) = (0,3).
Read det(A) = 3 in the panel: the shaded unit square has become a parallelogram with three times the area.
Keep a=2, b=−1, c=1 and slide d down to −0.5. det(A) reaches 0 and the whole grid collapses onto a single line.
Push d to −1. det(A) is now −1: the area is unchanged in size, but î and ĵ have swapped their turning order, so the plane has been flipped.
Set a=1, b=1, c=0, d=1, a shear. Only one dashed eigen-line remains, along the x-axis, with eigenvalue 1: those arrows slide along themselves without turning.
Set a=0, b=−1, c=1, d=0, a quarter-turn. The panel reports no real eigenvector directions, because every arrow turns.
